name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to accounts when passwords or PINs are unknown. A system may be configured to lock out accounts after a certain number of failed attempts.
detection: Monitor authentication logs (e.g. Windows Event ID 4625, Linux /var/log/auth.log) for bursts of failed authentication attempts from a single or distributed IP sources.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts and local network infrastructure devices to identify accessible services and potential attack targets.
detection: Monitor network telemetry and firewall flow logs for rapid connections or connection attempts across a broad range of ports.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries, including PowerShell, Windows Command Shell (cmd.exe), and Unix shells.
detection: Monitor process creation events (e.g. Sysmon Event ID 1) with command line arguments for unusual parent-child process relationships.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (e.g., HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend in with normal network traffic and avoid detection by network monitoring systems.
detection: Analyze outbound web traffic for regular beaconing intervals, rare user-agents, dynamic DNS domains, and unusually large payload transfers.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
detection: Monitor for anomalous user behavior, such as logins from unusual IP geolocations, odd hours, or concurrent sessions across disparate physical locations.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send phishing messages with malicious attachments or links to gain initial access to victim systems.
detection: Inspect inbound email gateways and monitor endpoint process spawning from email client executables.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password, from the LSASS process or SAM database.
detection: Monitor process access events targeting lsass.exe (e.g. Sysmon Event ID 10 with PROCESS_VM_READ permissions).
